slides.headline: India's 'blue bull' is not a bull.
slides.sub: The nilgai is an antelope, among the largest in Asia

slides.headline: The name means blue bull
slides.body: Nilgai comes from the Hindi nilgaw, 'blue bull', after the adult male's coat. It is an antelope, in the same family as cattle.

slides.headline: Only the males turn blue
slides.body: Females and young are yellow-brown. Only adult males turn blue-grey, and only males carry horns, about 20–25 cm long.

slides.label: top of the nilgai's weight range
slides.body: Nilgai weigh 120–240 kg and stand 120–150 cm at the shoulder, among the largest of the Asian antelopes.

slides.headline: Foothills to farmland
slides.body: In India nilgai range from the Himalayan foothills south to Mysore, usually in herds of about 10. They may damage crops where they live.

slides.headline: Least Concern, and stable
slides.body: IUCN lists the nilgai as Least Concern (2016), with an estimated 70,000–100,000 mature animals in India, Nepal and Pakistan and a stable trend.

caption:
India's 'blue bull', the nilgai (Boselaphus tragocamelus), is not a bull at all. It is an antelope.

Even its scientific name is a mix-up: it borrows the Latin for ox and Greek words for deer, goat and camel. Nilgai were also released in Texas about 1930 and still live on large ranches there.

Swipe to meet it properly. Sources on the last slide.
